---
title: "How do I compare before-and-after measurements from the same subjects?"
---

## What the question asks

How do I compare before-and-after measurements from the same subjects?

## Steps in RStudio

1. Confirm the before and after observations belong to the same units.

2. Compute each change.

3. Run t.test(after,before,paired=TRUE) and interpret the mean change.

## Runnable example

```{r}
before <- c(12,14,13,11,15,16,14,12)
after <- c(14,15,15,11,16,17,16,13)
change <- after-before
print(change)
print(mean(change))
print(t.test(after,before,paired=TRUE)$p.value)
```

## Interpret the result

The mean change is computed from paired differences. The test evaluates whether the population mean change differs from zero under its assumptions.

## Check before using real data

Keep each before value aligned with its own after value. Missing one side of a pair requires explicit handling.
